description: Capability surface of the NVFP4 paged-KV MSA decode kernel on compute capability 10.0/10.3. Each row is one HEAD GEOMETRY a deployment can present: num_qo_heads and num_kv_heads are read at runtime by the parametric kernel family and by the binding, so the rows enumerate the geometries that have been EXECUTED against the FP32 reference on device, not the geometries the kernel body is compiled for. head_dim and page_size are different in kind -- both are compile-time constants of both kernel bodies (the MMA K extent, the 128 B shared-memory swizzle, the output row stride, the whole shared-memory map), so a value not listed for them must never reach the kernel. Batch size, per-request KV length, block-table width, query length, causality, TOP-K and the two outer strides of the selection tensor are NOT listed: the kernel is parametric in all of them and restricting them would make the capability unreachable rather than route it somewhere faster.

parametric_axes.batch_size: any positive value; the cluster width is a pure function of batch_size * num_kv_heads and all four widths are precompiled
parametric_axes.seqlen_q: any positive divisor of the q row count; seqlen_q == 1 gets its own instantiation, everything else shares the general one
parametric_axes.seqused_k: any non-negative per-request length, heterogeneous across the batch, including partial final blocks and zero
parametric_axes.max_blocks: the block-table row width is a runtime argument
parametric_axes.causal: both, applied as a right-aligned limit
parametric_axes.topk: any value in [1, 32]. The ceiling is structural, not a policy: every selection slot is one lane of warp 0's compaction ballot in the parametric family (general::kSelectedCapacity), so a 33rd slot would be owned by a thread outside the ballot and dropped without a diagnostic. topk 16 additionally selects the pinned family and the CuTe-DSL scored_geom fast path; every other value is served by the parametric family.
parametric_axes.q2k_indices_outer_strides: any non-negative strides; only the innermost (top-k) dimension must be dense. Both kernel families take the head and token strides as arguments, so the transposed view of a token-major (total_q, num_kv_heads, topk) selection buffer is read in place and no consumer has to materialise a contiguous copy per step.

kv_cache_layout.note: The four inputs are strided views over one packed page pool and are consumed in place; the byte offsets between their base pointers are asserted, because shape, dtype and stride cannot tell four views of one page apart from four unrelated allocations, and the V-scale swizzle is invisible to all three.
kv_cache_layout.page_bytes_note: the tp=1 page. page_bytes = 2 * num_kv_heads * page_size * (head_dim/2 + head_dim/16); the four region offsets below scale with num_kv_heads the same way. Both kernel families take page_bytes, the data head stride and the scale head stride as ARGUMENTS and derive every address from them.

instantiation_families.note: The translation unit holds two families that compute the same function. This is a LATENCY split, not a capability one: nothing below narrows what the API accepts, and a call that misses the pinned envelope is served by the parametric family rather than refused.

compile_time_in_both_families.head_dim: general::kHeadDim sizes the MMA K extent, the 128B shared-memory swizzle, the output row stride and the whole shared-memory map; it is a constant of both kernel bodies, not an argument
compile_time_in_both_families.gqa_group_ceiling: general::kHeadCapacity = 16 bounds the group ABOVE; the group itself is a runtime argument (heads_per_kv) and the body guards every per-head site with it

read_at_runtime_but_pinned_by_the_bindin.page_size: the kernel body reads it and handles a partial page tile, but the binding requires 128 because the packed page map (page_bytes 73728) is derived from it -- widening this needs the CACHE WRITER to move, not the kernel

pinned.additional_runtime_condition: a batch of exactly 32 whose page pool holds fewer than 32 pages per request takes the parametric family; a serving pool is millions of pages, so this only separates undersized test pools
pinned.mirrored_in_python_as: flashinfer.msa_ops._nvfp4_decode_sm100.selects_pinned_path, which the binding cross-checks against its own derivation so the two copies cannot drift apart in silence

head_geometry.note: The four rows are MiniMax-M3's tensor-parallel ranks. vLLM shards the attention heads as num_heads = num_attention_heads // tp and num_kv_heads = max(1, num_key_value_heads // tp), replicating the KV heads once tp exceeds num_key_value_heads, and sizes the paged cache from the per-rank count (num_head_slots = 2 * spec.num_kv_heads). So the PAGE SHRINKS with the rank and every byte offset below is a function of num_kv_heads, not a constant.
head_geometry.max_gqa_group_reason: general::kHeadCapacity -- the parametric body runs one warp per query head inside a 512-thread CTA and sizes four shared-memory arrays by it. A group above 16 is refused by name.
head_geometry.fast_path_note: Only the tp=1 row (64/4/group 16) reaches the pinned CUDA family and the CuTe-DSL scored instantiations. Every other row is served CORRECTLY by the parametric family, which is the same function and, on the tp=1 rows where both were measured, about 1.29x slower. That is a latency statement about a geometry with no faster binary, not a capability one.
head_geometry.tensor_parallel_8_status: NOT LISTED, and the omission is deliberate. vLLM replicates the KV heads once tp exceeds num_key_value_heads, so tp 8 presents 8 query heads over 1 KV head -- GQA group 8. THIS kernel could serve it: the parametric family reads the group at runtime and 8 is under general::kHeadCapacity. The PREFILL kernel could not; its group is a tile shape (kQueriesPerTile * kTopK <= kHashSize with exact equality at 8 * 16 == 128). MSA over an NVFP4 cache needs both halves and there is no fallback for either, so a geometry only decode can serve would be a cache the prefill attend cannot read -- selected at startup and fatal on the first prefill. Listing the row is what would ship that, so it is not listed.
